cards.head: Trump called anyone saying artificial intelligence, not superintelligence, the enemy.
cards.body: The US president posted it a week after ordering federal agencies to use his term. Asked in parliament, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Japan keeps saying AI for now.

report_refs.excerpt: President Trump has declared on Truth Social that anyone who says "artificial intelligence" instead of "super intelligence" is an enemy of the White House.

cards.cat: Politics and government / Musk vs India
cards.head: Elon Musk accused Indian tycoons of blocking Starlink; India's government denies it.
cards.body: Musk, who runs SpaceX and its Starlink satellite internet, says Starlink has waited five years. India's ministry says Starlink and two rivals all await security clearance, calling the claim baseless.

report_refs.excerpt: Elon Musk, who heads SpaceX and the satellite internet service Starlink, accused unnamed "oligarchs" of blocking Starlink in India and asked whether Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries, is "the real boss of India", while India's government calls the claim of unfair treatment baseless.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / OpenAI sales
cards.head: OpenAI told investors its yearly sales pace is $20 billion below what it said before.
cards.body: An unnamed source says the gap comes mostly from comparing OpenAI with rival Anthropic. Anthropic counts cloud partner sales, OpenAI does not; a pace is monthly sales times twelve.

report_refs.excerpt: OpenAI has told investors its yearly revenue pace for September was almost $50 billion, well below the roughly $70 billion it had signalled earlier.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / WTO trade
cards.head: The World Trade Organization doubled its 2026 trade growth forecast on AI demand.
cards.body: Trade in AI goods like chips and servers rose two thirds from January to June. They made almost half of all trade growth, offsetting damage from the Middle East war.

report_refs.excerpt: The World Trade Organization more than doubled its 2026 forecast for growth in world goods trade, saying the AI investment boom is offsetting damage from the war in the Middle East.

cards.head: AI firm Anthropic now scans open-source code, readable by all, for flaws for free.
cards.body: Projects that opt in get scans by its strongest AI; nobody checks the flaw reports. Anthropic says some reports may be wrong; some projects already drown in AI bug reports.

report_refs.excerpt: Anthropic has launched a free service that uses its strongest AI models to scan open-source software for security flaws.

cards.head: OpenAI says it shut down Russian and Iranian groups using ChatGPT for fake writers.
cards.body: The Russian-linked group invented a think-tank head; the Iran-linked one planted almost 100 articles. The articles ran under fake journalists' names; OpenAI names no government agency behind either group.

report_refs.excerpt: OpenAI says it shut down Russian and Iranian influence networks that used ChatGPT to invent journalists and a think tank and place their stories in real news outlets.

cards.cat: Energy and infrastructure / Gas by truck
cards.head: Oracle is trucking natural gas to its AI data centres while it waits for pipelines.
cards.body: Trucked gas ran a Utah site a year and now feeds a Texas OpenAI campus. Analysts put trucked gas at about four times the usual price; Oracle did not comment.

report_refs.excerpt: Oracle is trucking compressed natural gas to its AI data centers to get power while it waits for pipelines.

cards.head: Humanoid robots directed traffic and guided tourists in a trial in Hangzhou, China.
cards.body: Only the maker, Chinese robot firm Deep Robotics, describes the trial of its DR02 robots. The firm says they handled busy crossings in rain, to free staff for tasks needing judgment.

report_refs.excerpt: Chinese robot maker Deep Robotics has tested its DR02 humanoid robots directing traffic and guiding tourists on busy Hangzhou streets.

cards.head: Walmart's warehouse robots break down too often and cannot handle its big boxes.
cards.body: After a decade, Walmart is still automating most of its roughly 200 US warehouses. Executives say fewer warehouse workers will be needed in time, without layoffs.

report_refs.excerpt: Walmart's decade-long, multibillion-dollar effort to run its warehouses with robots has been slowed by breakdowns, redesigns and trouble with boxes and large goods.

cards.head: Google unveiled its new top AI model, Gemini 4 Argon, first for security experts.
cards.body: Trusted experts get it without Google's usual cyber limits; paying developers follow after safety tests. Google claims top scores in coding, finance, law and security, from its own tests.

report_refs.excerpt: Google has unveiled Gemini 4 Argon, a new top-tier AI model, but is releasing it first only to a small group of trusted cyber defenders.

cards.head: Scientists say AI firm Anthropic overstated its find of a possible gene-editing tool.
cards.body: Anthropic said last month its AI found a DNA pattern that may edit genes. Copenhagen researcher Mario Rodríguez Mestre says his unpublished work shows it; he cannot prove copying.

report_refs.excerpt: Scientists say Anthropic's claim that its AI agents found a possible new gene-editing system is early and overstated, and a Copenhagen doctoral researcher says his unpublished work describes the same thing.

cards.cat: Ethics and law / USA Today sues
cards.head: USA Today's publisher sued OpenAI, saying it copied hundreds of thousands of stories.
cards.body: The publisher and its local papers say OpenAI trained AI on their articles without asking. They seek over $250 million; The New York Times also sues; OpenAI had not responded.

report_refs.excerpt: USA Today's publisher has sued OpenAI for copyright infringement, seeking more than $250 million in damages.

cards.head: A Google chatbot questioned patients before urgent visits and needed no safety stop.
cards.body: Boston hospital doctors watched all 98 completed chats live and never had to step in. The study, paid by Google's parent, tested only safety, not whether patients got better.

report_refs.excerpt: A Google medical chatbot that interviewed patients before urgent primary-care visits needed no safety stops in 98 supervised chats, in what researchers believe is the first real-world study of its kind.

cards.head: A US charity plans to record Gaza classrooms and have AI flag 'hateful' speech.
cards.body: Dr David Hasan, founder of the charity Gaza Children Village, described the plan last month. A board member and a partner aid group raised privacy concerns; families may not know yet.

report_refs.excerpt: A US charity running schools in Gaza plans to record classroom conversations and use AI to flag "hateful" speech, which has drawn privacy and ethics concerns.

cards.cat: The Fun Side / Robot hits host
cards.head: A Colombian streamer's own robot whacked him on the head during a livestream.
cards.body: Streamer Westcol turned his back while rehearsing a dance with the robot on air. He says it cost about $100,000; in earlier tests it kicked a display case apart.

report_refs.excerpt: A Colombian streamer was hit on the back of the head by his own robot during a livestream.

entries.head: Google showed a Gemini AI helper for firms that works across apps, now in testing.

report_refs.excerpt: Google has announced a single Gemini agent for business customers that can take on work tasks across apps and devices, though it is still in private preview.

entries.head: A humanoid shop robot shown in Tokyo could stock Japanese convenience stores from 2027.

report_refs.excerpt: A robot maker working mainly in Thailand showed a humanoid built for shop work in Tokyo and plans to put it in Japanese convenience stores from as early as 2027.

entries.head: US Democratic senators say some tech giants mislead on AI data centre costs and jobs.

report_refs.excerpt: A year-long Senate investigation led by Democratic senators argues that some big tech companies are misleading the public about the costs and benefits of AI data centers.

entries.head: San Francisco rents rose a quarter, blamed on the AI boom; eviction notices rose 44%.

report_refs.excerpt: The AI boom is pushing San Francisco rents sharply higher, and eviction notices in the city are up 44% on last year, the Guardian reports.

cards.head: AI investors now want results, not promises, after OpenAI's lower sales figure.
cards.body: OpenAI's sales pace came in lower; data-centre firm Firmus dropped its share sale. Watch if OpenAI raises money at a $1.4 trillion value; not financial advice.

report_refs.excerpt: Heavy borrowing by Oracle, Broadcom, SpaceX and other companies to pay for AI is pushing up the cost of insuring their debt against default, Bloomberg reports.
OpenAI has told investors its yearly revenue pace for September was almost $50 billion, well below the roughly $70 billion it had signalled earlier.
Firmus, an Australian data-centre company backed by Nvidia, has cancelled its planned $5 billion share sale after investors held back.
SoftBank's chief executive is reportedly asking Gulf investors for up to $100 billion to fund a new wave of AI investments.
The World Trade Organization more than doubled its 2026 forecast for growth in world goods trade, saying the AI investment boom is offsetting damage from the war in the Middle East.

cards.notice: General news and commentary. Not financial advice or an investment recommendation.
